AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO ENERGY AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS
AMENDED BY RESTORING TO PREVIOUS PRINT 1163A

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to net energy metering for
fuel-flexible linear generator electric generating equipment
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1163

SPONSOR: BENJAMIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public service law, in relation to net energy meter-
ing for fuel-flexible linear generator electric generating equipment

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill would provide parity in "net energy metering" for fuel-flexi-
ble linear generators under Public Service Law § 66-j.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill would amend Public Service Law § 66-j throughout
to provide parity in net energy metering or fuel-flexible linear genera-
tor electric generating equipment. Specifically, the bill would amend:

*§ 66-j (1)(a) to include fuel-flexible linear generator electric gener-
ating equipment in the definition of "customer generator";

*§ 66-j (1)(f) to clarify that this type of technology is included with-
in the definition of "micro-combined heat and power generating equip-
ment";

*§ 66-j (1)(i) to add a definition of "fuel-flexible linear generator
electric generating equipment" and "fuel flexible linear generator" to
mean an integrated system consisting of oscillators, cylinders, elec-
tricity conversion equipment and associated balance of plant components
that directly convert the linear motion of the oscillators into elec-
tricity and which has a combined rated capacity of not more than two
thousand kilowatts;

*§ 66-j(2)to clarify that an electric corporation shall provide for the
interconnection to fuel-flexible linear generator electric generating
equipment;

*§ 66-j(3) to make conforming changes to add fuel-flexible linear gener-
ator electric generating equipment to the list of technologies for which
each electric corporation must develop a model contract and file a rate
schedule, terms, and conditions for net metering;

*§ 66-j(4)to make conforming changes to add fuel-flexible linear genera-
tor electric generating equipment to the list of technologies for which
an electric corporation must use net metering to measure the charge for
the net electricity supplied by the corporation and provided to the
corporation by a customer-generator;

*§ 66-j(4) to make conforming changes to add fuel-flexible linear gener-
ator electric generating equipment to safety standards that electric
corporations must establish;

Section 2 of this bill would provide for an immediate effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2019, the New York passed historic climate legislation aimed at
reducing greenhouse gasses economy-wide, but especially from the burning
of fossil fuels in the electric generation sector.  Fuel-flexible tech-
nology to reduce emissions is needed now more than ever. One such fuel-
flexible technology is the fuel-flexible linear generator, a technology
similar to fuel cells that is capable of running on clean and environ-
mentally friendly fuels such as hydrogen and bio-diesel. Fuel-flexible
linear generators use a low-temperature reaction of air and fuel to
drive magnets through copper coils to efficiently produce electricity.
As a result, high-efficiency generation can be achieved with near-zero
NOx emissions, while maintain full dispatchability to the grid while
using hydrogen or renewable fuels. However, while the current law recog-
nizes other, similar technologies such as fuel cells, the Public Service
Law does not encompass this cutting-edge technology. This bill would
amend the Public Service Law to cover this technology for net metering
purposes, allowing customers to benefit from clean, dispatchable, gener-
ation, ensuring a more stable, secure, and environmentally responsible
electric grid, and bringing New York's ambitious carb on neutrality
goals within closer reach.

New York has previously provided parity-recognition when it added this
technology to the list of equipment eligible for sales tax relief

(FY-2017-18 Budget, and most recently, property tax relief pursuant to
Chapter 325 of the Laws of 2018.)

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-20: S.8203/A10268-A

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This Act shall take effect immediately.
